messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-prod-420' GPU utilization 100% (sustained 7m). Queue length 142. Top tenant: CastleTech (95% of queued requests). Severity: P1.
ryan: paging oncall (handing off to maya).
pagerduty: Incident triggered -> paging maya.
maya: ack'ing, joining. oncall here. pulling logs.
ryan: quick context — this is CastleTech's dedicated pool, they are on reserved capacity, sudden spike in batch rerank workload. customer CS looped in (leo).
leo: castletech engineering reached out, they say a nightly job started misbehaving around 02:12 UTC. asked them to pause but they haven't confirmed.
maya: can we see pod-level GPU usage and which jobs are hot?
anita: pulling runtime telemetry now — listing top containers by GPU mem usage.
(anita posts snippet)
```
2025-09-14T02:20:03Z pool=eu-west-1-prod-420 tenant=castletech pod=rt-gen-7 gpu_mem=15.8GB util=98% cmd="/opt/redwood/bin/serve --model xlarge"
2025-09-14T02:21:10Z pool=eu-west-1-prod-420 tenant=castletech pod=rt-rerank-3 gpu_mem=15.9GB util=99% cmd="/opt/redwood/bin/rerank --batch 128"
```
maya: yep rerank pod spiking. the pool has no spare capacity assigned. options: 1) enable burst-to-shared (fast) 2) throttle tenant concurrency (fast) 3) move some jobs to standby model variant (requires coord) 4) call customer to pause job. thoughts?
ryan: preference is preserve customer SLA for dedicated pool if contract allows burst. but CastleTech is high tier, we could enable a short burst and then bill/notify. need approval from product?
leo: CastleTech approved emergency burst earlier in onboarding? Checking contract — they have reserved 8 GPUs, no automatic burst. They asked for manual approval last quarter for occasional bursts. I can authorize a 15 minute burst if needed.
anita: technical note — our shared spare capacity in eu-west-1 is currently 60% free but that would mix workloads. If we enable burst, we should set a fallback: if shared utilization >70% stop bursting.
maya: ok practical plan: 1) throttle incoming concurrency to reduce queue while we enable controlled burst for 12 minutes; 2) notify CastleTech with ETA; 3) monitor tail latency and CPU/GPU. I'll execute in that order.
ryan: +1. add a temporary guardrail to avoid noisy neighbor risk.
leo: castletech notified via email thread, they asked to continue if it keeps things stable. gave verbal OK.
maya: running throttle command now.
```
# cap concurrent tokens per-tenant
redwoodctl pool tenant update --pool eu-west-1-prod-420 --tenant castletech --max-concurrency 12
```
maya: throttle applied, queue dropped from 142 -> 98 in 2m.
anita: enabling burst to shared for up to 12m with guardrail.
```
# enable short burst into shared spare capacity with stop condition
redwoodctl pool burst-enable --pool eu-west-1-prod-420 --tenant castletech --duration 12m --stop-if-shared-util-above 70
```
anita: API returned: burst session id=b6f3a, routed 6 extra GPUs from shared pool.
maya: seeing additional nodes come up and pods rebalance. logs: "attached 6 burst gpus -> pool eu-west-1-prod-420"
(anita posts log snippet)
```
2025-09-14T02:26:40Z pool=eu-west-1-prod-420 burst=b6f3a attach=+6 shared_util=42%
2025-09-14T02:27:11Z pool=eu-west-1-prod-420 pod=rt-rerank-3 moved_to_node=nvidia-a100-22 util=88%
```
maya: tail latency improved 500ms -> 120ms for most requests. queue down to 12.
ryan: excellent. set a timer for 10m to review before auto-stop.
leo: notifying CastleTech that we've applied a 12m burst and throttled concurrency, they'll see reduced errors. updating ticket.
(anita): monitoring shared pool utilization; it's stable at 46%.
maya: small hiccup: one rerank job retried aggressively, causing temporary spike back to 85% GPU on a single pod — manually evicted that pod to redistribute load.
```
kubectl delete pod rt-rerank-3 -n pool-eu-west-1-prod-420
```
maya: pod restarted and came up on a burst node, util normalized.
ryan: decision point at +10m: either extend burst or require CastleTech to pause nightly job. what's the ask from CS?
leo: CastleTech prefers we keep service uninterrupted for now; they're debugging their pipeline but need time. they asked for another 10m extension.
anita: we can extend 10m, but add stricter max-concurrency (8) and enable autoshrink if shared_util > 65%.
maya: I propose: extend 10m, set max-concurrency=8, enable autoshrink stop-if-shared>65, and open a follow-up with Eng-Platform to propose a longer-term quota rule for dangerous nightly jobs.
ryan: sounds reasonable. annotate incident with decisions & cost estimate.
(anita runs)
```
redwoodctl pool burst-extend --session b6f3a --extend 10m --set-tenant-max-concurrency 8 --stop-if-shared-util-above 65
```
anita: extended. new shared_util 49%. queue now 4.
maya: setting post-incident actions: 1) engage platform to add a policy to catch high-throughput rerank jobs in dedicated pools; 2) run customer runbook with CastleTech to add rate-limiter; 3) bill adjustment note. I'll create the follow-up.
ryan: preparing handoff to night oncall in 25m. summary looks good.
leo: CastleTech confirmed they will patch their nightly job and asked for a short post-incident note. I'll own customer comms.
(anita): burst session b6f3a set to auto-shrink at 02:52 UTC.
maya: monitoring 5m after extension — stable. lowering severity to P2.
incident-bot: Update: Severity -> P2 (mitigated). Actions: throttle applied, burst enabled (session b6f3a), pod eviction, extension.
ryan: closing active paging. handoff: night-oncall is @sara (not in thread), jira INC-4589 created for follow-ups with eng-platform and billing.
leo: will DM castletech with summary + expected invoice note.
maya: leaving runbook notes in the incident doc: commands used, logs, timestamped metrics, and recommended platform rules.
incident-bot: Incident status: resolved -> monitoring.
ryan: thanks team.
